name: shell-operator-742b3baf-blind29
instr:
# Diagnosing shell-operator's injected misbehaviour without a test suite

I run an installation that launches small scripts in response to what happens in a cluster, and it now gets a great many things wrong at once. Nothing about the cluster changed and nothing about my scripts changed. The repository has received 29 separate undocumented edits. What follows is everything I could pin down from the outside, grouped by what I was doing at the time.

Getting it going at all is the first trouble. Pointing it at a folder of scripts that plainly exists on disk comes back as a failure, as though no path had been handed over, so nothing is loaded and no initial work is ever lined up. The TLS listener that accepts callbacks from the cluster refuses to come up too: with a certificate and key pair in place and readable, the call to bring it up hands back an error instead of succeeding quietly. On the command line, the client certificate authority path I give for the endpoint that reviews changes before the cluster accepts them has no effect, ending up holding whatever the surroundings had rather than what I typed, and the client certificate authority path I give for the endpoint that translates a resource between stored revisions is dropped the same way. Everything else on that same command line — the certificate, key and authority paths, the failure policy, the ports and the addresses for both endpoints, and the client, patching, logging and introspection options — arrives exactly as
